claim_summary: Operator-conducted ARIA self-audit (2026-05-10) identified two architectural-quality gaps in the kernel-internal silencing/tracking discipline: (1) pressure._phase2_effective_context wraps both the deferred trust import and the trust function calls in a single `except Exception` block, silently swallowing real data errors from `trust.trusted_gap_keys` and `trust.ref_status_by_feedback_id` that feed pressure evaluation feeding operator decisions; (2) cycle.py:54-56 documents `pr_lifecycle` phase as emitting a placeholder governance event because the cycle entry point doesn't carry a proposal_id, but the placeholder carries no `# aria-debt:DEBT-...` source-side marker and no entry in `aria-state/architectural_debt.jsonl`, in violation of CONTRACTS.md §6.6 + IDENTITY.md §3.6 short-term-workaround-as-tracked-debt schema (debts without owner+deadline are forbidden). Anchors close in two fix commits + one verification commit. Tier V (1072/1072 unittest discover green) closes the finding.

evidences.summary: _phase2_effective_context broad `except Exception` swallows trust function data errors; pre-fix code path.
Source-side comment acknowledges pr_lifecycle phase emits placeholder governance event; no aria-debt: marker, no DEBT-* record.
§6.6 Architectural Debt Record schema: debts without owner+deadline are forbidden; source-side marker `// aria-debt:DEBT-XXX` adjacent to workaround required.
§3.6 Rule 3 short-term workarounds are architectural debt with owner + due date.

Top-level `from .trust import ref_status_by_feedback_id` proves trust module load is unconditional in production; the only legitimate ImportError surface in pressure._phase2_effective_context is the circular-import edge.
Top-level `from .pressure import close_pressures_from_signals` confirms the circular chain pressure -> trust -> feedback -> pressure that necessitates a deferred function-level import in pressure.

facts: pressure.py:481-487 wraps both `from .trust import ...` and `trusted_gap_keys(paths)` + `ref_status_by_feedback_id(paths)` in one `except Exception: return set(), {}` block.
Top-level `from .trust import ...` in reverify.py and learning.py demonstrates the trust module loads cleanly outside the circular edge — no other call site needs the broad swallow.
cycle.py:54-56 contains a NOTE explicitly stating `pr_lifecycle` emits a placeholder governance event with no real PR action, but the placeholder is not adjacent to any `# aria-debt:DEBT-...` marker.
`grep -rn 'aria-debt:' aria-kernel/ tools/aria-poc/` returns zero matches across the entire ARIA codebase despite the schema being defined in CONTRACTS.md §6.6.
ARIA self-audit is operator-conducted (manual, no originating skill or pressure event) and recorded as a process integrity check on 2026-05-10.

interpretations.text: The pressure swallow is small in isolation but has high observability multiplier: a real bug in trust derivation feeds an empty trusted_gap_keys() into pressure-state evaluation, downgrading pressures to `unknown` ref-stale silently. MEDIUM severity reflects the audit-path masking risk, not a confirmed live regression.

The cycle.pr_lifecycle placeholder is itself architecturally honest (it does not pretend to act); the violation is process: short-term workarounds without owner+deadline+marker grow louder, never quieter (CONTRACTS §6.6). Closure requires the marker + a debt record, not removal of the placeholder.

recommendation: Two fix commits + one verification commit. (1) Narrow pressure._phase2_effective_context except to ImportError; trust function calls leave the try block. (2) Add `# aria-debt:DEBT-2026-05-10-001` marker adjacent to cycle.py:54-56 placeholder note + write the debt record to `aria-state/architectural_debt.jsonl` with owner, deadline (2026-06-24, 45 days), root_cause_summary, short_term_action, permanent_fix_plan, source_marker. (3) Tier V mechanical re-run: `npm install` + `unittest discover` confirms 1072/1072 green; on success, F-006 status flips OPEN -> RESOLVED with closes_in_commit set.
